record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: For every infinite locally compact topological group that is not totally disconnected, do the four separable quotient variants all hold: existence of a non-trivial separable quotient group, existence of an infinite separable quotient group, existence of a separable metrizable quotient group, and existence of an infinite separable metrizable quotient group?

evidence.quote: Does every infinite non-totally disconnected locally compact group have a separable quotient group which is (i) non-trivial; (ii) infinite; (iii) metrizable; (iv) infinite metrizable?

artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of an ongoing research program on separable quotients of topological groups. Positive results are known for important subclasses: every infinite locally compact abelian group, every infinite compact group, and every infinite non-protodiscrete pro-Lie group admits an infinite separable metrizable quotient. However, the full problem for arbitrary non-totally-disconnected locally compact groups remains open, in parallel with the long-standing Banach–Mazur separable quotient problem for Banach spaces.

status_evidence.title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey lists Problem 16 on whether every infinite non-totally disconnected locally compact group has separable quotients of the four indicated kinds.
status_evidence.claim: The four-part question is posed as an open problem in the survey.

status_evidence.title: The separable quotient problem for topological groups
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes positive results for compact groups, locally compact abelian groups, and pro-Lie groups, but leaves the general locally compact (non-totally-disconnected) case open.
status_evidence.claim: Significant special cases of the problem are settled, but the general locally compact case remains open.
